sections.content: You know *aunque* from A2 Unit 28: it admits a fact that goes against what follows. With a real fact, use the indicative. This pattern is useful when you compare what the constitutions said with what happened.

items.spanish: Aunque Chile abolió la esclavitud en 1823, en Brasil continuó hasta 1888.
items.english: Although Chile abolished slavery in 1823, in Brazil it continued until 1888.

items.spanish: Aunque muchas mujeres lucharon en los ejércitos, no obtuvieron el voto.
items.english: Although many women fought in the armies, they did not get the vote.

items.spanish: Aunque las constituciones hablaban de libertad, muchas personas quedaron fuera.
items.english: Although the constitutions talked about freedom, many people were left out.

items.spanish: Aunque la ley era igual para todos, no todos tenían los mismos recursos.
items.english: Although the law was the same for all, not everyone had the same resources.

sections.content: *Aunque* can open the sentence or follow the main clause, and it uses the indicative for a real, known fact. A comma separates a sentence-opening *aunque* clause.
